topic.title: Resetting a Locked-Out Linux User Account from Single-User Mode
topic.shortdesc: Use single-user mode to regain access by remounting the root filesystem, resetting the password, and restoring normal boot settings.

body.p:
Explain prerequisites: console access (physical or out-of-band), authorization to perform recovery, and awareness of full-disk encryption constraints.
Outline the high-level flow: interrupt bootloader, enter single-user/emergency shell, remount root read-write, reset credentials, verify account state, and reboot.
Include safety notes: avoid changing unrelated system files, document actions for audit, and ensure you can revert boot parameter changes.
